newsitem.title: UK: Analyst sees sharp rise in China barley imports.
newsitem.headline: Analyst sees sharp rise in China barley imports.

text.p: Rising beer consumption but a stable barley production at home should turn China into a major barley importer by the year 2000, a leading analyst in the beer and barley malting sector said on Thursday.

"Beer consumption in China will rise until the year 2000 and it will have an impact on barley consumption. But barley production should remain flat, so barley imports are expected to grow," said Arend Heijbroek, food and agribusiness sector manager at Rabobank International of the Netherlands.

In a speech to the London conference of the International Grains Council, he predicted that Chinese barley imports would rise to 2.7 million tonnes in the year 2000 compared to 1.4 million tonnes in 1994.
Barley production was expected to remain steady at 4 million tonnes while beer consumption was seen rising to 220 million hectolitres from 155 million in 1994.
He also put Chinese barley consumption in the year 2000 at 6.7 million tonnes compared to 5.4 million in 1994.
